about: Pflaume is German for plum, and the name points to the roots of Hollerhorn’s fruit brandies. Distiller Karl Neubauer, who founded the distillery outside Naples with his wife Melissa in 2018, draws on his family’s ties to Austria and its schnapps tradition, alongside the French eau-de-vie method. Hollerhorn sits at the south end of Canandaigua Lake, and Karl builds his brandies around whatever the nearby farms harvest each season.

This one uses 100% German-variety brandy plums grown in Geneva, New York, on the north end of Seneca Lake. The fruit is fermented with several yeast strains, champagne yeasts among them, chosen to carry its aromatics, then double distilled in a pot still to no more than 160 proof. Unlike Hollerhorn’s unaged brandies, Pflaume rests in barrel; some batches have been aged in a cask that previously held bourbon and the distillery’s Old Growth maple spirit. Karl worked on the recipe for more than five years. Hollerhorn describes a floral, aromatic nose, an oily texture and a long finish of burnt sugar.
facts: 100% German-variety brandy plums from Geneva, NY
Double distilled in a pot still, to no more than 160 proof
Barrel-aged; some batches in an ex-bourbon/ex-Old Growth barrel
